crop.notes: right edge of the column is cut off; the last few letters of most lines are missing (e.g. 'Tom Allen Puts in a Wor[d]', 'Ex-Champion of A[merica]')

ocr.notes: gist and names readable; many character errors, and line ends missing because of the crop

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reprinted from the Clipper a letter in which Tom Allen disputed Joe Coburn's claim to be the only champion of America, saying he had challenged Coburn ten times without an answer.

metadata.notes: masthead reads 'Daily Democrat, Sunday Morning, February 12, 1871'; letter reprinted from the New York Clipper, dated St. Louis, January 27

facts.fact: Allen wrote to Frank Queen of the New York Clipper from St. Louis disputing Joe Coburn's claim to be the only champion of America and challenging Coburn
Allen said he had challenged Coburn ten times since coming to America and Coburn never answered
facts.quote: I have challenged Coburn ten times since I have bee[n in this] country, and he never answered any of my [challen]ges.

facts.fact: Allen offered Coburn $200 to withdraw from his match with Jem Mace and offered to stake $3,000 to fight Coburn on the same day, the 11th, fifty miles from Detroit

notes: Month of the proposed fight date is cut off ('the 11th of A...'). Allen signed as 'Ex-Champion of A[merica]'. Brackets in the quote mark letters lost at the crop edge.
